name: MathVista
description: MATHVISTA is a benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA), covering diverse mathematical reasoning types, tasks, and visual contexts.
creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
citeAs: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao. MATHVISTA: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. ICLR 2024.
rai:dataCollection: MATHVISTA was compiled from 31 source datasets: 9 existing multimodal MathQA datasets, 19 publicly available VQA datasets containing math-related instances, and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA). For MathQA datasets, each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples, yielding 2,666 examples total. For VQA datasets, the authors reviewed more than 70 datasets and selected 19 public datasets. They first applied heuristic rules to automatically select examples likely involving mathematical reasoning, yielding 4,949 VQA-format examples, then engaged three expert annotators to manually label whether these examples involved mathematical reasoning; majority voting and a 400-example cap per source dataset produced 2,739 examples. The three new datasets were created to address missing scenarios: logical reasoning on puzzle test diagrams, algebraic reasoning over functional plots, and scientific reasoning on academic figures. IQTest contains 228 examples sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms, FunctionQA contains 400 examples, and PaperQA contains 107 examples sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface. All questions in the new datasets were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Others
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data come from 31 source datasets, including 9 existing multimodal MathQA datasets, 19 existing publicly available VQA datasets, and 3 newly annotated datasets created by the authors: IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA. IQTest was sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms, and PaperQA used figures from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: PaperQA examples were sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface. Multimodal Bard evaluation dates ranged from Sep 8, 2023 to Sep 10, 2023, and GPT-4V evaluation dates ranged from Oct 7, 2023 to Oct 15, 2023.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select likely math-related examples based on numeric answers or quantity words in questions, followed by manual filtering with majority voting. For release, the dataset was split into testmini (1,000 examples) and test (5,141 examples). To construct testmini, the authors first randomly sampled questions with a threshold number of 4 for each source dataset, then randomly sampled remaining questions for each source dataset based on its proportion in the entire set.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, the authors designed heuristic rules to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates. Examples with numeric answers or containing quantity words in the questions were selected. This automatic filtration yielded 4,949 VQA-format examples, after which expert annotators manually labeled whether they involved mathematical reasoning. The dataset also underwent several quality checks to address unidentified errors. Answers for evaluation are normalized to required formats such as option letters, integers, floating-point numbers, or lists.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Examples were annotated with metadata including question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, visual context, and required reasoning skills. Metadata such as question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, and visual context were obtained from source dataset details. Coarse labels of mathematical reasoning were automatically obtained from source dataset details. To verify automatic annotation quality, expert annotators manually labeled mathematical reasoning categories for 1,000 examples from seven candidates. For selecting math-related VQA examples, three expert annotators manually labeled whether automatically filtered examples involved mathematical reasoning, using majority voting. For the three new datasets, all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields. Each new dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, and disagreements were resolved through discussion among the entire review team.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: The authors developed annotation tools with GUIs for labeling whether a problem involves mathematical reasoning, annotating the three new datasets, and labeling mathematical reasoning skills.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For the newly collected 736 questions, independent annotation by three reviewers resulted in a 99.2% inter-annotation consistency rate; only 6 questions exhibited disagreements, which were resolved through discussion. For labeling whether problems involved mathematical reasoning, the authors computed a Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775 among three annotators, indicating substantial agreement. For mathematical reasoning category labels, 94.1% of examples from automatic and human annotations had the exact same set of reasoning types, while 98.79% of individual labels were identical.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields; three expert annotators; qualified human annotators on Amazon Mechanical Turk with a satisfactory annotating history and a high school diploma or higher.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The answer labels for the test split will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination, and the authors will maintain an online evaluation platform. The benchmark is described as part of an ongoing research process, and the authors are committed to maintaining the datasets, refining potential data noise in response to community feedback, and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Language; grade level; educational attainment of human annotators
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to facilitate development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios and evaluate progress of foundation models on rigorous reasoning tasks. The paper states that AI agents with strong mathematical reasoning capabilities in visual contexts have real-world applications in education, statistical analysis, theorem proving, and scientific discovery. It also argues that MATHVISTA will play a critical role in developing general-purpose AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that source datasets are heterogeneous and annotations lack a unified format and structure because they were sourced from original data providers. It also notes that there may be gaps in representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. For few-shot experiments, the authors observe that some models are sensitive to bias in demonstrations.
rai:dataLimitations: The paper acknowledges several limitations: dataset coverage may have gaps in certain types of mathematical problems and visuals; the focus on mathematical reasoning in visual contexts spanning domains like science and college-level math makes high-quality data collection labor-intensive; scalability and generalizability to other domains remain concerns; only 85.6% of examples have annotations; annotations from original data providers lack a unified format and structure; and the study focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models. The benchmark also contains multilingual questions, including 6.57% non-English questions, which may add difficulty. The answer labels for the test split are not publicly released to prevent data contamination.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is a benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It is intended for model development validation and standard evaluation. The testmini subset of 1,000 examples is intended for model development validation or for those with limited computing resources, while the test subset of 5,141 examples is for standard evaluation. The benchmark is used to evaluate text-only LLMs, augmented LLMs, large multimodal models, and human performance.
